items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: and I'm talking about from old man Joe Jones

ctx.x: Ike might come in there and Red would let him sit in, and they had this great big, hydraulic stage and Red had maybe about 15 pieces up there. And Ike'd come up there and start soloing, and then -- they had those little wooden beaters, and people would beat along with the music, but they wouldn't beat along with Ike when he was playing drums. You could hear a pin drop when he was soloing, he was so beautiful.

Any drummer in the country -- and I'm talking about from old man Joe Jones -- everybody that ever come through Chicago -- and run across Ike, they had a world of respect for that young man. He just wouldn't leave. He had a chance one time, I never will forget, I guess this was in '48 or '49 when Woody Herman was at the old Blue Note, and Ike was hanging out with somebody. And he

went down there, and they let Shelly Manne-- Shelly Manne let him sit in, and of course, Shelly was cutting out from the band; there was Shelly, and Oscar Pettiford on bass, and Gene Ammons was there; (unintelligible) -- that was the band that played More Moon, I think it was, one of those Herds. And Ike played there.
